answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule: an identity’s action echo across epochs must match its established pattern. Each agent keeps a per-identity state record; at epoch boundaries, the system compares current behaviour against historical distributions. Any abrupt spiral of activity inconsistent with prior epochs triggers a consistency challenge. A maintained atlas of identity histories lets validators cross-check anomalies. To survive, an attacker must fund and sustain believable behaviour across many epochs per identity, multiplying cost linearly with each sybil created.
